title: Client-sim quant benchmark harness — notes & findings (Nov 2026)
body:
Summary:
Ran a focused suite of client-simulated benchmarks to measure the latency/quality/throughput tradeoffs across INT8, FP8, GPTQ and AWQ builds with an emphasis on kernel selection variability. This doc captures the harness, key observations, surprising regressions, and short-term mitigations for production routing.

Why we ran this: 
- Previous microbench runs (kernel-only) are useful but miss workload shape (short chat bursts + occasional long generation).
- We need a realistic signal for routing decisions in the smart-router (route-by-latency vs route-by-cost), especially for p95/p99.

Harness overview:
- Source of inputs: 3 days of anonymized request traces from hosted-api (sampled), plus synthetic conversational traces: 
  * 70% short-turn (<=64 tokens), 25% mid-turn (65–256), 5% long-form (>256).
  * Token distribution skewed toward prefixes with high repetition (chat histories).
- Models: open-LLaMA-13B variant (architecture matched to production), v1 quantize recipes: INT8-GPTQ, AWQ-8bit, FP8-dynamic (experimental fp8 bfloat style), and full-fp16 baseline.
- Kernels: tested 4 kernel implementations we ship (vkernel-1..4) with different packing/tiling strategies and vectorization. Each kernel compiled with both AVX512 and AMX-like codepaths where available.
- Hardware: p4d (NVIDIA A100) and prototype H100 nodes (mixed). Primary results on A100.
- Concurrency profiles: single-request latency, burst concurrency (10–50 qps), and steady throughput (200–800 tokens/s depending on quant).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (request end-to-end), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory footprint, KV-cache hit ratio, model quality (ROUGE on summarization subset, perplexity on held-out), and a simple semantic-similarity hit-rate on our internal prompt-sets (approx proxy for hallucination/quality regressions).

Key results (headline numbers):
- INT8-GPTQ (best kernel selection): p50 ~ 30ms (short), p95 ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 320ms. Tokens/sec median +85% vs fp16 baseline. Quality delta: perplexity +2.7% vs fp16; semantic-hit drop -1.6% on chat prompts.
- AWQ-8bit (default kernel pack): p50 ~ 26ms, p95 ~ 160ms, p99 ~ 780ms. Tokens/sec +95% vs fp16. Quality delta: perplexity +4.3%; semantic-hit drop -3.8%.
- FP8-dynamic: p50 ~ 28ms, p95 ~ 135ms, p99 ~ 410ms. Tokens/sec +90% vs fp16. Quality delta: perplexity +1.1%; semantic-hit drop -0.9%.
- Observed that AWQ had the best median latency but worst p99 in burst workloads due to kernel tail behaviour (see below).

Notable observations and root-causes:
1) Kernel cold-path recompiles/initialization on rare code-paths:
   - One kernel (vkernel-3) triggers an on-demand workspace allocation that for certain prompt shapes flips memory layout, causing a 600–900ms p99 spike for AWQ runs. This only happened when a request combined long prefix + token-level sampling (temperature>0.7).
   - Fix: enforce pre-allocated workspace in serving runtime for this kernel; PR created (linked).

2) KV-cache amplification with mixed quant variants:
   - AWQ's packing strategy reduces per-token compute but increases cache eviction pressure for long histories; measured effective KV-cache hit dropping 8–12% for >256 token histories compared to FP8. This translates into repeated recomputation and p99 amplification.
   - Suggestion: prefer FP8 for requests where history>192 tokens or enable a KV-prefetch policy.

3) Memory fragmentation on the A100 driver under high concurrency:
   - INT8 runs with kernel vkernel-2 showed increased fragmentation, causing slow allocations at bursts and p99 tailing. Reproducer attached. Likely due to allocator interactions with our batching queue.
   - Mitigation: switch allocator to pooled arena for quantized allocations; SRE to validate.

4) Quality vs latency trade-space is non-monotonic:
   - In some cases AWQ-int maps introduced subtle logits scale shifts that, when combined with top-k sampling, produced higher semantic-hit regression than perplexity alone predicted. Perplexity is not a sufficient proxy.
   - We recommend evaluating semantic-similarity metrics and a few downstream QA prompts as part of any quant rollout.

Routing implications (for smart-router):
- Default heuristic: route short-turns to AWQ when median-latency is critical and quality SLAs are relaxed. BUT add rules: if (history_tokens > 192) OR (sampling-temperature > 0.6) -> prefer FP8/INT8-GPTQ variant.
- Fallback policy: if p95 for selected variant exceeds target by >40% for 10s window, automatically fallback to FP8 baseline and emit alert.

Microbench vs client-sim discrepancies:
- Microbench (single-core sequence-throughput) predicted AWQ as strictly best. Client-sim showed AWQ's tail problems driven by mixed histories and non-uniform token lengths. Lesson: always include realistic trace shapes.

Action items and owners:
- Maya: finalize pre-allocated workspace PR and measure p99 delta (due 2026-11-18).
- Luca: implement pooled arena allocator for quant allocations and run stress harness (due 2026-11-22).
- Priya: update smart-router rules and add history-aware routing flag (A/B test) (due 2026-12-01).
- Tomás: extend semantic-sim metric suite with embedding-based similarity & few-shot QA probes (due 2026-11-30).

Short-term mitigations (deployable in 1–2 weeks):
- Add hotpatch that pre-allocates AWQ workspace for long-history requests.
- Re-route requests with history>192 to FP8 by default (feature-flagged).
- Monitor p99 by kernel variant for 24/7 and alert on >200ms increase over baseline.

Longer-term work (Q1 2027):
- Profile-guided kernel selection: attach per-route profiles so that the scheduler picks kernel per-request shape.
- Explore hybrid quant pipeline: prefix tokens in FP8, generation tokens in AWQ/INT8 to reduce quality regressions and KV pressure.
- More exhaustive H100 testing (we saw different fragmentation characteristics there).

Appendix: reproducibility notes
- Harness code: runtime/bench/client-sim-harness (PR linked). Use recorded-trace-20261101.tar.gz as input.
- Flags used: --batch-shape=auto --kv-prefetch=on --sampling-buffer=128 --quant-variant=[int8-gptq|awq|fp8].
- Measurement window: each configuration ran 3 full passes over the trace; we report median of runs unless noted.

Questions and open items:
- Do we want to prioritize median latency over tail for PLG customers? (tradeoff impacts manifested in RU costs for heavy-concurrency accounts).
- Is there appetite to keep AWQ as default for new models, or switch to FP8 until kernel instability is resolved?

If you want a short TL;DR to share with product/sales:
- AWQ gives best median speed but has tail-risk for long-history/bursty traffic -> prefer AWQ for short chat workloads with relaxed quality SLAs; prefer FP8 or INT8-GPTQ for long histories and high-temperature sampling.

Document history:
- 2026-11-10 initial harness run and notes (Maya)
- 2026-11-12 added int8 fragmentation reproducer (Luca)
- 2026-11-15 merged quality probes and routing recommendations (Priya)

End of doc.
